Quick technical addendum — high level recommendations to include in the proposal:
1) Quantization: start with 8-bit PTQ as a baseline for medical prompts, then test 4-bit QAT/FP8 hybrid for non-critical scoring paths. In our experience:
   - 8-bit PTQ: negligible quality delta for most clinical QA prompts, safe default.
   - 4-bit: can introduce tokenization-level hallucination risk on rare, structured medical tables; requires prompt-level evals and a small calibration set.
2) Batching & Caching: enable continuous batching with a soft latency SLO of 120ms p50; use prefix/KV caching for recurrent patient-session context (we recommend a per-session KV cache TTL of 12h for MedAssist). This reduces token compute by ~18–30% in similar workloads.
3) Dedicated pilot cluster: recommended to avoid noisy neighbor variance; configure a 3-GPU pilot pool (A10G-equivalent) with autoscale off for the test window.
4) Metrics & QA: define acceptance gates — latency p50/p95, prompt-level accuracy on a 200-sample eval set, and a manual review of hallucination cases.

I'll attach a short benchmark CSV showing expected per-token cost deltas across quant profiles.
Aditya
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
